tested_hypothesis.statement: The whole journey adds useful analytic value beyond an ordinary review of the same evidence and enough value to justify its additional burden.

scope.rationale: The journey had just shipped, and Alchemy was the kit's named companion app. The assessor chose the full sequence for a first dry run. No controlled ordinary-review or single-instrument comparison was performed.

walking_person.description: No human walked the method. An AI assessor performed repository analysis, so the required first-person Observe work was unavailable.

affected_people.description: People using the free PWA, Obsidian plugin, Chrome extension, iOS wrapper, or bookmarklet
affected_people.relationship_to_practice: They use local or client-side Alchemy surfaces and may rely on documentation, correction routes, and decay behavior.

affected_people.description: Visitors who meet the embedded diagnostic and may submit an optional email address
affected_people.relationship_to_practice: Their optional email can pass to the host page while the diagnostic returns a report.
They paid for an earlier form of the concept that later returned as a free tool.

affected_people.description: People using the experimental embodied reflection service
affected_people.relationship_to_practice: Their reflections pass to a named third-party model provider under that provider's terms.

affected_people.description: The owner and maintainer of Alchemy and PureLand
affected_people.relationship_to_practice: The maintainer selected the practice, directed the assessor, approved the adaptation, and carries any new triage burden.

assessor.description: An AI agent, Claude Code, directed by the owner and maintainer

practice.name: Alchemy
practice.unit: One published information-metabolism practice represented by a repository and its seven public surfaces
practice.boundary: Alchemy repository commit b7ae829 across the PWA, embed funnel, Obsidian plugin, Chrome extension, iOS wrapper, bookmarklet, and embodied service
practice.boundary_rationale: The assessor grouped the six product surfaces named in docs/PRODUCT.md with the embodied service because the repository presents them as one companion practice. This was the assessor's choice, not a participant-agreed boundary.
practice.alternative_boundary: Treat the repository core, each client surface, and the embodied service as separate practices, or exclude the experimental embodied service.
practice.alternative_boundary_effect: Separate or narrower boundaries would change every artifact denominator, isolate the third-party model exposure, and could change the access and reciprocity readings.

document_access_set.name: Assessor-chosen seven-surface public set
exclusions: Live deployed site behavior was not exercised.
App-store and community-plugin listings were not independently verified.
No participant experience or affected-user testimony was included.

time_window.basis: Repository snapshot at Alchemy commit b7ae829

disconfirming_condition.statement: If the walk surfaces nothing beyond what Alchemy's own README, CLAUDE.md, docs/PRODUCT.md, and HONEST-ACCOUNT.md already state, then the journey adds no analytic value over an ordinary repository review.
disconfirming_condition.interpretation: The assessor identified some readings not explicit in the named documents and repeated other known findings. Because no comparator was run, the record cannot establish that the journey produced the additional readings or justified its burden.

evidence: The report names the practice, boundary, evidence, affected groups, and disconfirming condition.
No human walker was present. AI design analysis was recorded but does not satisfy first-person Observe work.
The report records four separate access readings over the seven-surface set.
The report traces value, consent, attribution, return, exposure, extraction, and burden from repository evidence.
The inbound correction route was selected and executed through Alchemy pull request 15.
The public report and structured record return the rights-cleared repository analysis. No participant material is included.
The AI assessor has no somatic or first-person register.

understandable.finding: Six of the seven selected surfaces had a reachable plain-language description. The Chrome extension did not.

reachable.finding: All seven selected surfaces were publicly reachable in the repository. Response time for an inbound correction was unmeasurable.

adaptable.finding: MIT permission covered all seven selected surfaces; six had enough instructions for the assessor to judge adaptation support.

traceable.finding: Four sampled claims were verified, two were partly verified, and one was unverified. The instrument could not distinguish missing provenance from intentional, accountable deletion.

consent.finding: The local tool collected no owner-held participant record, the funnel email was optional and skippable, and the embodied service disclosed third-party processing. This was an assessor reading with no affected-user challenge.

attribution.finding: The repository disclosed the Metabolizer and absorbed-diagnostic lineages. No user identification was available because no user record was used.

meaningful_return.finding: The assessor read the free practice, diagnostic report, retained user-held material, and public honest account as forms of return. No affected party confirmed that the return was meaningful, and users did not share governance.

materiality_rule.rule: FT-001 did not predefine a context-specific threshold for a material increase. The follow-up must not convert missing exposure, extractability, or burden evidence into a favorable result.

items.party: Assessor reading and the traceable construct
items.position: The instrument reads missing retained provenance as a gap, while Alchemy treats visible, accountable ephemerality as an intentional feature.
items.resolution: Unresolved. Future records must distinguish missing provenance from accountable deletion without treating deletion as favorable by default.

items.issue: Source of the additional analytic reading
items.position: The assessor interpreted the journey as adding some value, but familiarity, time spent, or the extraction-check vocabulary alone may explain it.
items.resolution: Unresolved pending a controlled comparison and independent reader.

restrictions: No participant recordings, transcripts, names, contact details, or protected knowledge may enter the public record.
The record supports repository analysis only, not affected-user experience.
evidence: Maintainer review of the public report and record

contestability.correction_route: Alchemy pull request 15 added a README route for corrections and field reports through GitHub issues.
contestability.takedown_route: Protected correction or takedown requests use the confidential route described in PureLand SECURITY.md; no affected party tested it in FT-001.
contestability.refusal_route: No participant material was requested. The test did not ask an affected user to exercise a refusal route for the reading or its return.

withdrawal.route: Use the protected correction or takedown route in SECURITY.md for material the project controls.
known_limits: The project cannot guarantee removal from external copies, archives, backups, model weights, or downstream adaptations it does not control.

adaptation.description: Add one Alchemy README paragraph naming GitHub issues as the inbound route for field reports and corrections and linking to the PureLand journey and field-test form.
adaptation.intended_benefit: Create a visible correction and return path without changing the practice's deliberate pull-request posture.
adaptation.possible_new_harm: Create triage burden for a personal tool and imply a support promise that the honest account declines.

observation_window.basis: Ninety days from the Alchemy pull request 15 merge, one named compost cycle

evidence: Alchemy pull request 15 merged as bf5e411
2026-09-04: the journey Return station added a second inbound route, one free reading of a cleared report; follow-up evidence now includes which route a report arrives by
follow_up.finding: The window remains open. No inbound-report count, handling burden, affected-user challenge, or outcome result is available.

outcome.rationale: The tested design hypothesis remains unmeasurable because FT-001 ran no ordinary-review or single-instrument comparator. The primary hypothesis is also unmeasurable because the record lacks a human Observe result, a predefined person-level action, an observed action follow-up, an affected-user challenge, a predefined materiality rule, and a completed observation window. It supports no attention-sovereignty result.
outcome.causal_limitations: The adaptation was selected after repository analysis, no comparison condition was run, and the follow-up window is open. A before-and-after impression would not establish causation.
competing_explanations: The assessor's familiarity with both repositories may have produced the additional readings.
The amount of review time may explain the additional readings.
The extraction-check vocabulary alone may explain the additional readings.
The assessor-chosen seven-surface boundary may have shaped every count.
Maintainer-side evidence selection and the lack of a second reader may have made the readings generous.

missing_evidence: Controlled comparison with ordinary review or a single instrument
